generic: Freeze-Dried Live Attenuated Hepatitis A Vaccine
cls: Live attenuated viral vaccine - active immunisation against hepatitis A
pharm: A freeze-dried preparation of live attenuated hepatitis A virus (e.g. H2 or L-A-1 strain) that induces protective anti-HAV antibodies, providing active immunity against hepatitis A infection
quick: Single 0.5 mL (>=6.5 log10 CCID50) dose subcutaneously after reconstitution
Live vaccine - generally avoid; weigh risk/benefit, defer if possible
Use with caution; data limited (inactivated HAV vaccine preferred if needed)
Use caution in significant liver disease; immunise as indicated
Immediate hypersensitivity; injection-site and systemic reactions
summary: Freeze-dried live attenuated hepatitis A vaccine is a single-dose vaccine (using an attenuated HAV strain such as H2 or L-A-1) that produces active immunity against hepatitis A. It is reconstituted with the supplied diluent and given as a single 0.5 mL subcutaneous injection (potency typically >=6.5 log10 CCID50 per dose), generally to children from 12-18 months of age and to susceptible older children and adults. A single dose induces seroconversion in the great majority of recipients and provides long-lasting protection; it is widely used in national immunisation programmes in some countries (notably China and India). As a live vaccine it is generally avoided in pregnancy and in significantly immunocompromised persons. It is not represented in openFDA (live attenuated HAV vaccines are not US-licensed; the US uses inactivated HAV vaccines); dosing follows the manufacturer's insert and WHO/national immunisation guidance.
indications: Active immunisation against hepatitis A virus infection in susceptible children (usually from 12-18 months) and adults
Pre-exposure prophylaxis in those at risk of hepatitis A

dosage.d: Single 0.5 mL reconstituted dose (potency typically >=6.5 log10 CCID50)
dosage.t: Subcutaneous injection, usually in the upper arm/deltoid region
dosage.n: Reconstitute with supplied diluent and use promptly

dosage.d: Some programmes use a single dose; certain schedules give a second dose
dosage.n: Follow the specific product insert and national schedule

admin: Reconstitute the freeze-dried vaccine only with the diluent supplied; the reconstituted vaccine should be clear and used promptly
Administer by subcutaneous injection, typically into the deltoid region (upper arm); follow the product insert
Do not mix in the same syringe with other vaccines; use a separate site if co-administering
Have adrenaline and resuscitation facilities available for the rare anaphylactic reaction; observe after injection
Discard reconstituted vaccine if not used within the time specified by the manufacturer
moa: The live attenuated hepatitis A virus replicates to a limited extent in the recipient, presenting viral antigens to the immune system and eliciting a humoral immune response with production of protective anti-HAV (IgG) antibodies and immune memory. This active immunity neutralises wild-type hepatitis A virus on subsequent exposure, preventing infection and disease. Because replication is limited and attenuated, immunity is generated without causing clinical hepatitis in immunocompetent recipients.

absolute: Known severe hypersensitivity to any vaccine component or after a previous dose
Significant primary or acquired immunodeficiency / immunosuppression (live vaccine)
Acute severe febrile illness (defer until recovery)
relative: Recent immunoglobulin/blood product administration (may blunt response)

preg: As a live attenuated vaccine, it is generally contraindicated or to be avoided in pregnancy because of a theoretical risk to the fetus; vaccination should usually be deferred until after delivery. If hepatitis A protection is needed during pregnancy, an inactivated HAV vaccine or immunoglobulin is preferred. Weigh individual risk and benefit.
lact: Data on use during breastfeeding are limited. Use with caution; if hepatitis A immunisation is required in a breastfeeding woman, an inactivated HAV vaccine may be preferred. The decision should weigh maternal need against limited safety data.
renal: No dose adjustment is required in renal impairment.
hepatic: Use with caution in patients with significant liver disease; immunisation against hepatitis A is in fact recommended for many patients with chronic liver disease, but for those who are immunocompromised an inactivated vaccine may be preferred over a live product.

major: Immunosuppressive therapy (high-dose corticosteroids, chemotherapy, biologics) - may diminish the immune response and increase risk from the live vaccine
moderate: Recent immunoglobulin or blood-product administration - may reduce the antibody response; separate appropriately
Other live vaccines - give simultaneously at separate sites or space by about 4 weeks
interactions.diagnostics: May transiently affect anti-HAV serology interpretation

emergency: Anaphylaxis with airway compromise or shock

monitoring: Observation for immediate hypersensitivity reactions for about 15-30 minutes after injection
Ensuring contraindications (immunosuppression, pregnancy) are screened before dosing
counsel: This vaccine protects against hepatitis A, a liver infection spread by contaminated food and water
A sore arm, mild fever or tiredness for a day or two is normal
Tell the clinic if you are pregnant, have a weakened immune system, or have had a serious reaction to a vaccine before
Stay for the short observation period after the injection
Seek urgent help for any rash, facial/throat swelling or breathing difficulty after vaccination
Keep your vaccination record and attend any booster appointment advised
pk: Protective anti-HAV antibodies typically develop within about 2-4 weeks of a dose
Peak antibody titres develop over several weeks after vaccination
Not applicable - vaccine induces durable active immunity rather than measurable drug levels
Long-lasting protection (years) after a complete course
Store freeze-dried vaccine at 2-8 C protected from light; do not freeze the diluent; use reconstituted vaccine promptly
pearls: Live attenuated single-dose HAV vaccine (e.g. H2/L-A-1 strain) - widely used in China and India; the US uses INACTIVATED HAV vaccines
Generally avoided in pregnancy and immunosuppression because it is a live vaccine
Given subcutaneously after reconstitution; a single dose seroconverts the majority with durable protection
Not represented in openFDA (not US-licensed) - dosing follows the manufacturer's insert and WHO/national schedules
For immunocompromised patients or pregnancy needing HAV cover, prefer an inactivated vaccine or immunoglobulin
missed: This vaccine is typically a single dose; if a scheduled (or booster) dose is missed, it can be given at the next opportunity - the series does not need to be restarted. Follow your local immunisation schedule.
overdose: Overdose is highly unlikely with a single-dose presentation. Inadvertent administration of more than the recommended dose is managed by observation and supportive care; no specific antidote is required.
